THE PROBLEM THIS EXISTS FOR.

The card arrives 2026-09-19.

A first day spent discovering that piecemeal is a first day not spent training.

The teacher is outputs/t107/labels_ours.parquet and it scores gold-58 0.8976.
data/llm_labels.csv scores gold-58 1.0000 -- not because it is better but because its 58 is_gold rows carry the gold values themselves.

--res is validated in every mode: the manifest and the verify both print the training command, and a resolution that cannot be trained is not worth printing anywhere.
Cached hashes: a 21.9 GB re-read is minutes, and re-running a manifest is exactly what you do after adding one file.
The cache key is (path, size) -- a file that changed without changing size keeps a stale hash, which is why --rehash exists and why the corpus sizes are pinned by the contract above.
The HF weight cache is a directory of content-addressed blobs;
the blob IS the payload and its name is its sha256.
Recorded per blob so --verify can check the bytes, not just that something with the right name exists.
A pinned file whose size is wrong must never be hashed into a manifest: the far end would then verify successfully against a truncated original.
1. the repository (brings src/, $GOLD, this script, the manifest)
2. the corpus -- 20.4 GiB, gitignored, the long pole.
Trailing slash on both sides, and -P so an interrupted copy resumes instead of restarting.
3. the teacher -- 197 KiB, gitignored, and the one file that decides whether the run means anything. rsync does not create the parent.
4. optional: the timm weights, so 08:00 does not wait on huggingface.
-a keeps the blob/snapshot symlink layout, which is what makes it a cache.
The destination is the PARENT: a source without a trailing slash lands as a subdirectory of it, which is what puts the cache back where timm looks.
5. at the far end
The manifest is data, and data can be edited.
Every corpus size it carries is cross-checked against the shape derivation FIRST, so the far end trusts the contract rather than the file it was handed.
Without this, a manifest with a truncated corpus size would verify perfectly against a truncated corpus.
A carry entry is fatal: nothing else brings it here, so a mismatch is a broken copy.

A git entry that differs means this checkout is a different commit -- loud, but fixed with git, not with rsync, and conflating the two would bury a corrupt 16 GB transfer under a source-drift warning.
Occupancy from the card, never from pgrep -f: a watcher that names the pattern it waits for matches itself, which deadlocked five shells here and later killed a live fold (CLAUDE.md).

THE PROBLEM, measured 2026-09-18.

src/coat_model.py's CoatMIL and the public notebook's RaptorClassifier are mathematically identical -- the same LayerNorm, the same Sequential(Linear(F,256), Tanh, Dropout, Linear(256,12)), the same clsW/clsb, the same einsum('bkn,bkf->bnf'), and backbones built with the same num_classes=0, in_chans=3, global_pool='avg'.
They are not the same state dict, because ours keeps the head as a submodule and theirs holds it as direct attributes:
ours head.norm.weight head.att.0.weight head.clsW head.clsb theirs norm.weight att.0.weight clsW clsb
Their loader is model.load_state_dict(ck['model'], strict=True).
So a checkpoint we train is refused by the pipeline that would score it, and the failure lands at the end of an eight-hour Kaggle run rather than at the start.
Eight characters of prefix, one wasted day.
This module is those eight characters, with the proof beside them.
WHAT THE NOTEBOOK ACTUALLY READS from a checkpoint (load_model, cell 47):
ck = torch.load(pt_path, map_location='cpu', weights_only=False) arch = ck.get('arch', arch_default) ck_res = int(ck.get('res', res_default)) model.load_state_dict(ck['model'], strict=True)
Three keys: model, arch, res.
res is not decoration -- it is the resolution our arm is EVALUATED at, so a checkpoint trained at 224 and shipped without it would be scored at their default 384 and silently measure something else.
export_checkpoint writes all three.
WHY THE REFERENCE CLASS IS EXTRACTED AND NOT RETYPED.
raptor_classifier_source pulls the class text out of the notebook itself.
A hand-copied reference would drift from the notebook the moment either changes, and the test would keep passing -- the defect class this project logs as "a check that passes for the wrong reason".
If their class changes, the extraction changes with it and the equivalence test fails, which is the whole point of having one.

The subtler failure, and the one that cost two drafts: cell 47 groups arms by (img, slots, span, k_eval) and decodes each group's studies ONCE, then resizes per arm to res inside eval_windows.

So img is the DECODE size -- a new value is a whole extra pass over the test set, against T105's measured 429-434 min and a registered 495-min cap -- while res is the only thing the model actually sees.

Nothing here checked that.
THE DEFECT (audit 2026-09-18, reproduced below).
coatnet_rmlp_ generates its relative-position bias from an MLP over a grid fixed at build time.

Their build_backbone passed no img_size, so timm built the architecture default -- 384, i.e. 576 positions -- while load_model read ck['res'] and eval_windows then fed the model 224 px windows, which are 196 tokens.
Every forward raises.
WHY IT WAS SILENT, and why it is worth this much machinery.
arm_probs is pre-filled with 0.5, load_model SUCCEEDS, and the forward raises inside a per-arm per-study try/except that prints FALLBACK and continues.
The kernel reaches COMPLETE, the VOID banner prints -- it prints at import, before the arms run -- and our column stays a constant 0.5 for every study.
A constant column is invariant under the notebook's rank-percentile routing, so the submission is exactly the parent with our member zero-weighted: it measures the REMOVAL of a member.

T112's registered rule reads a low score as "<= 0.934 REJECT, our arm is worse", so a resolved negative about our own architecture would have entered the record from a run in which our arm never executed once.
WHY EVERY EXISTING GUARD MISSED IT.
test_coat_export proves the checkpoint->notebook join on resnet18, which has no grid constraint.
scripts/t112/dry_run.py uses resnet18 too.
push_arm.py proves the state dict LOADS.
The builder checks res % 32 == 0 -- arithmetic, not a forward.

Not one of them built the backbone the kernel builds and pushed a window through it, and their own four arms all evaluate at 384 = the default, so ours is the first member that could ever have exposed it.

So this check does the one thing none of those did: it takes the notebook's OWN build_backbone/load_model/RaptorClassifier, applies the builder's own grid_edit, loads a REAL CoAtNet checkpoint at a res that is not 384, and forwards a real window.
The control is the same thing UNFIXED, which must raise -- otherwise this check is passing on a backbone that never had the constraint.

Corpus access and the window bag, for the adopted CoAtNet arm.

The corpus is published preprocessed (dreaddevelopment/knee-raptor-corpus plus -ext, CC0-1.0): two uint8 arrays of shape (N, 44, 336, 336) that together hold 4,407 studies, with a companion (N, 44) mask marking which slices are real. Nothing here decodes a DICOM.
A study becomes a bag of windows, not a stack of slices.
Each window is three physically consecutive slices stacked as the three channels of one RGB image -- most of the benefit of a 3D model at the cost of a 2D one.
Training draws k window centres at random every epoch, so the same study presents differently each time;
the resampling is the augmentation, and apart from a mild intensity jitter nothing else is augmented.
No flips: laterality is signal here, not nuisance (Medial/Lateral are separate findings).
Two contracts this module exists to enforce, because breaking either is silent:
Row order. Part 1 precedes part 2 in the volumes, the masks and the ids alike.
Sorting any one of them independently mis-pairs studies with images and the run still trains, just on scrambled supervision.
The teacher is llm_labels_raw.csv, never llm_labels.csv. The latter carries gold values in its 58 is_gold rows, so a model trained on it scores gold 1.0000 and means nothing.
Those same 58 rows are the right source of validation truth -- the trap is using them to train.
The normalisation the adopted inference notebook applies to every window (eval_windows, cell 47): x = (x - _MEAN) / _STD with the ImageNet constants, under NORM = "imagenet".
This module divided by 255 and stopped, which is a real mismatch and not a stylistic one: measured 2026-09-18, their inputs carry ~4.48x our standard deviation and a -0.24 mean shift.
A model trained on [0, 1] and scored on that is being shown a different distribution, and -- worse -- the kernel runs clean and the low score reads as "our arm is worse" rather than as a bug.
imagenet is also what sw_in12k_ft_in1k was pretrained under, so it is the distribution the frozen features expect.
The default stays none so the 2026-09-18 fold remains exactly reproducible;
choosing imagenet is an explicit, pre-registered change.
The two corpus parts as one (N, D, H, W) read-only view.
Never concatenated on disk: 22 GB of copying to serve reads that are always a single study.
Indexing is by global row, part 1 first.
Memory-map both parts.
Refuses a half-staged corpus.

A run supervised by one of those is not wrong at train time -- the gold studies are held out either way -- but every claim made about "what our teacher is worth" would be measuring gold against itself.

The public trainer this replaces assumes a 24 GB card and offers no gradient accumulation, so on anything smaller the only lever is --bs, and dropping the batch is not a cheaper version of the recipe -- gradient noise, the effective learning rate under OneCycle and the normalisation statistics all move together.
Accumulation is the whole point of this file: --bs 2 --accum 4 puts the same 8 studies into every optimizer step as --bs 8 does, on 6 GiB instead of 16.

Why every cache is redirected: C: is full. uv's download cache, uv's managed Python, the Hugging Face cache (the pretrained CoAtNet weights) and TEMP all default to C:, and a torch install alone needs ~3 GB of download cache.
The tool-specific ones are made permanent for this user, so later training runs and Claude Code sessions use the SSD too.
TEMP is deliberately NOT made permanent: every Windows program would then depend on this drive.

Installing from a cache on C: into a venv on this drive copies files OFF C:, so a full C: is not a problem here.

The training curve for one CoAtNet fold: gold-58 AUC and loss against epoch.
python scripts/coat_curve.py # the 224 fold python scripts/coat_curve.py --run outputs/t112/<tag>.json # any other
WHAT IS PLOTTED, AND WHY IT IS AUC AND NOT ACCURACY.
The competition metric is the mean of twelve column ROC-AUCs, and it is the only per-epoch figure a coat fold records: coat_train.py writes hist as (ep, loss, gold_auc, minutes).
There is no per-epoch accuracy to plot and no way to recover one -- only the argmax and the last checkpoint survive a fold, so epochs 0-15 cannot be re-scored under any other statistic.
Accuracy at the argmax is a number per label, not a curve, and scripts/roc_curves.py is the figure for per-label behaviour.
THE GUARD, in the idiom roc_curves.py uses.

A figure of a different run than the text beside it is worse than no figure, so this REFUSES rather than draws when the file disagrees with itself: best_gold_auc must be the maximum of hist, the recorded epoch count must match the history, and --expect (when given) must match the number the board and PROGRESS.md carry.
The drawn numbers are read from the run's own JSON, never retyped here.
WHAT THE FIGURE SAYS, on the 224 fold.

The metric climbs steeply to epoch 4, peaks at 0.8848 at epoch 7, and then drifts sideways-to-down for eight more epochs while the loss keeps falling monotonically to 0.632 -- the classic shape of a model that has stopped learning the target and started fitting the teacher's noise.
Half the fold's 3.5 hours bought nothing.

READ THAT SHAPE WITH T115/H3 IN HAND. Every CoAtNet fold to date, this one included, trained with persistent_workers=True, which froze set_epoch in the workers -- so the per-epoch window resampling that coat_data.py calls "the augmentation" never happened, and the model saw ONE fixed draw of 12 of ~42 legal window centres for all 16 epochs.
A fixed augmented copy of the corpus is exactly the setup in which a model plateaus early and then overfits, so the flat tail is not safely readable as "16 epochs is too many".
The caption says so on the figure, because a curve travels further than its commit message.
